bands.text: For women, a score of 3 or more shows drinking at a level that can harm your health. Cutting down or taking a break brings clear benefits.

audit.text: It's the 3-question short version of the 10-question AUDIT alcohol test developed by the World Health Organization, asking about how often and how much you drink. Each question scores 0–4; the total is 0–12. For women, a score of 3 or more points to drinking at a level that can harm health, and 8 or more to high risk. It's a screening test; it doesn't diagnose.

sexual.text: Alcohol slows the nervous system; when you drink a lot, arousal and orgasm can become harder. Decisions made while drunk also increase the risk of unprotected sex.
Drinking too much for a long time can upset your hormone balance, affect your periods and fertility, and damage the liver and nerves, lowering sexual desire.
The link between light to moderate drinking and sexual health isn't clear in research; however, according to the World Health Organization there's no safe amount of alcohol for health.
